correctness.rationale: Adjacent-label conjugation flips the descent at those positions except when the two images are the same adjacent pair. That exceptional pair is either two fixed points (no descent) or a two-cycle (one descent); class symmetry gives the stated Fulman formula and, on derangements, Cov(f(K),D)=Cov(f(K),C₂)/n. Marking a specified two-cycle factors out one factor θ and an independent size-(n−2) Ewens derangement, proving the exact transformed identity. Deletion of label n from a longer cycle is invertible by inserting it after one of n−1 labels; deletion of a two-cycle containing n leaves n−2 labels and one of n−1 possible partners. These produce the positive mixture of K_(n−1) and 1+K_(n−2), with common θ. From K₂=K₃=1, inductively K_(n−2)≤st K_(n−1)≤st 1+K_(n−2) orders the mixture endpoints; placing K_n between them and using the first inequality closes the induction at the next size. The lower endpoint has positive mass at one (a long cycle), while the upper endpoint does not. Thus every strictly increasing transform separates their finite laws, and positive mixture weights give a strict size-biased expectation gap. At n=2,3 the cycle count is constant. For unrestricted uniform permutations the marked fixed-point pair and the marked two-cycle each have expected count 1/2 and shift the residual cycle count by two and one respectively, yielding −1/(2n), including n=2. The repaired attribution has no effect on these hypotheses, identities or signs.

value.rationale: The stochastic sandwich is a finite-size structural order, not a new computation of one scalar covariance. It shows why marking a two-cycle increases every increasing cycle-count score in expectation and explains positive covariance with ordinary descents uniformly in θ. The result is useful even without counting the identity-transform case or prior descent/marking formulas as new; it does not claim full joint association.
